---
title: "Monte Carlo error with dependent draws"
subtitle: "1.18 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 21, and the postrank vignette m6"
description: "Finite-sample uncertainty of pair probabilities estimated from a stationary two-state Markov chain."
---

Correlated Markov chain draws carry less information about $\pi_{AB}$ than independent draws, inflating estimator variance so nominal independence-based error bounds fail far too often.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Stay .99.** Naive iid SD is .0500 vs. exact .376; the .05 iid bound (±.148) fails in 1,602 of the 2,000 chains (.801; exact .804), at least .370 from never switching.
- **Stay .99, chain-aware.** Exact SD is .376 (variance .141) vs. .0500 (.00250) iid, matching 1.77 independent draws (long-run 1.01).
- **A stuck chain.** Chain 7 never switches; 720 chains never switch.
- **Stay .50.** Independent draws fail in 10 of the 2,000 chains (.00500; exact .00352).
- **1,000 draws.** Precision equals 10.6 independent draws; the ±.0468 bound fails in .777 of chains (exact .770).
- **postrank's chains.** Open *Data*: `pr_toy_mcmc` gives share .172 vs. .2 (MCMC MCSE .0576 vs. .00835 iid; R-hat 1.0905, ESS 42.95) and loss .248 vs. 4/15 (.191 to .296 by chain).

```{=html}
<details class="prx-prose-details">
<summary>Source and package notes</summary>
<p>The stationary two-state chain with $\pi_{AB} = 1/2$ is restated from the postrank theory book, ch. 21 (“A finite-sample coefficient bound for dependent draws”); exact finite-sample variances and tail probabilities follow from the transition probability alongside outcomes counted across chains simulated in the browser. In postrank, <code>postrank_iid_bounds()</code> refuses MCMC draws, and <code>postrank_diagnose()</code> reports R-hat, ESS and an MCMC MCSE for them (vignette m6, “Monte Carlo uncertainty and diagnostics”).</p>
</details>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank); law <- attr(pr_toy_mcmc, "law")
mc <- postrank_draws(pr_toy_mcmc, regime = "mcmc", chains = 4L, warmup_per_chain = 0L, thin = 1L, declarations = law$declarations)
postrank_diagnose(mc, pairs = data.frame(entity_i = "A", entity_j = "B", criterion_id = "k1"))$summaries$pair_1$diagnostics   # values: rhat 1.090465, ess_bulk 42.95484, mcse_mean 0.05764243 (1.0905, 42.95, .0576)
```
:::

Standalone: [embed/chain-draws.html](../../embed/chain-draws.html), for example `?stay=.95&draws=200` or `?preset=aware&theme=dark`.
